skill.name: agentdb-learning-plugins
skill.description: Create and train AgentDB learning plugins for reinforcement learning workflows, including Decision Transformer, Q-Learning, SARSA, Actor-Critic, and related training patterns.
skill.summary: Build AgentDB learning plugins for reinforcement learning agents.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code fences or illustrative TypeScript and JSON examples. The confirmed issue is repeated use of unpinned npx agentdb@latest commands, which can execute remote package code at runtime. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin agentdb commands to a reviewed version and avoid @latest in marketplace examples.
Require explicit user confirmation before any assistant runs the documented npx commands.
Document that .agentdb/learning.db may contain task data and should stay out of source control.

content.value_statement: Training agent behavior with reinforcement learning can be complex and repetitive. This skill guides AgentDB plugin creation, configuration, training, evaluation, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains nine AgentDB learning algorithms and their intended use cases.
Shows CLI workflows for creating, listing, and inspecting learning plugins.
Provides API examples for storing experiences and training models.
Outlines training workflows from data collection to evaluation.
Covers advanced patterns such as replay, multi-agent training, and incremental learning.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for convergence, overfitting, and slow training.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 and AgentDB through the agentic-flow package.
Assumes users understand basic reinforcement learning concepts.
Does not verify package versions or install dependencies automatically.
Examples need adaptation for each environment, reward design, and data shape.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Learning Agent
use_cases.description: Use AgentDB templates to choose an algorithm and create a first plugin for a task environment.

use_cases.title: Design a Training Workflow
use_cases.description: Map experience collection, model training, and evaluation into a repeatable workflow.

use_cases.title: Compare RL Approaches
use_cases.description: Review supported algorithms and select a method for offline learning, discrete actions, or continuous control.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starter Algorithm
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new learning plugin.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an AgentDB learning algorithm for my task. My environment has [state type], [action type], and [reward signal].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Plugin Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an AgentDB learning plugin for [use case]. Include the template choice, training data shape, evaluation metric, and setup commands.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Training Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentDB training workflow for [problem]. Suggest changes for convergence, overfitting, batch size, and validation strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Agent Learning
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow design for shared training.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-agent AgentDB learning workflow for [agents] and [shared objective]. Include experience storage, replay, model updates, and evaluation.

output_examples.input: I need a Q-Learning plugin for a grid-world task.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends the Q-Learning template, a discrete action design, an exploration schedule, and an evaluation loop for episode rewards.

output_examples.input: My learning model is overfitting after short training runs.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests validation splits, lower training intensity, memory optimization, and closer checks on reward diversity.

output_examples.input: I want offline learning from historical agent logs.
output_examples.output: The skill points to Decision Transformer, explains experience formatting, and outlines training and evaluation steps without live environment interaction.

best_practices: Pin package versions before running AgentDB CLI commands.
Start with clear reward signals and simple evaluation metrics.
Keep local learning databases out of source control.
anti_patterns: Do not run npx commands from the skill without user approval.
Do not train on production data before reviewing privacy requirements.
Do not choose an advanced algorithm before defining states, actions, and rewards.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps create AgentDB learning plugins for reinforcement learning and agent improvement workflows.

faq.question: Which algorithms are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Decision Transformer, Q-Learning, SARSA, Actor-Critic, Active Learning, and other listed AgentDB methods.

faq.question: Does it install AgentDB for me?
faq.answer: No. It documents CLI and API workflows, but package installation should be reviewed and confirmed by the user.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Yes, but basic reinforcement learning knowledge helps users choose algorithms and interpret training metrics.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What security caution matters most?
faq.answer: The examples use npx agentdb@latest, so users should pin versions and approve commands before execution.
